AWARD/JUDGMENT FACTUAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS 1.
A DAR was filed on 06/01/2024 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of the parties.
The said DAR was related to a motor vehicular accident dated 14/08/23 in which one Ansh Kumar S/o Sh. Prakash Yadav (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained grievous injuries.

Subsequent to filing of DAR present petition U/s 166 r/w Section 140 of M.V. Act was seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 30 Lakhs in respect of injuries sustained by petitioner in a road traffic accident which took place on 14/08/2023 at about 4.30 PM at a spot Outer Ring Road, Service Road near Wazirabad Flyover falling within the jurisdiction of PS Wazirabad was filed.

As per this petition, at the relevant time the petitioner was in process to board the bus bearing registration no.
DL-1PC-6663 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") suddenly the driver of the offending vehicle/ R-1 closed the gate of the bus negligently and moved the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and as a result of petitioner fell down on the road and his left leg and ankle crushed by the offending vehicle.

It is further stated that the the injured was admitted in BJRM hospital by the Duty Marshal of the offending PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.11.12 14:15:10 +0530 vehicle from where he was referred to LNJP Hospital where the surgery was performed in his left leg.
It is further stated that the said accident was caused due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver / R-1 who closed the door negligently and drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
An FIR no. 842/2023 PS Wazirabad U/s 279/337 IPC was registered wherein it is stated that the accident took place on account of rashness and negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
As per petition, the petitioner was 12 years old at the time of accident and was a student.

Petitioner claims that the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent Ansh Kumar (I)(Fir842/2023Wazirabad) vs Sachin Kumar (Oic) on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86767763/
3 manner.
R-1 is the driver of the offending vehicle.
R-2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
R-3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
2. A joint written statement was filed by R-1 and R-2 wherein it is claimed that the accident took place due to the negligence of the petitioner herself.
On merits, the averments of petition have been denied in toto.

However, it is stated that at the relevant time the offending vehicle was covered by an insurance policy issued by R-3/ Insurance Company, therefore, the liability, if any, is to be discharged by R-3 only.
3. R-3/Insurance Company filed a reply in which it denied the contents of petition.
However, it is admitted by R-3/ Insurance Company hat

at the relevant time the offending vehicle was covered by an insurance policy issued by itself in favour of PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:

ISSUES 4. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed for consideration on 15/05/2024 by this Tribunal:-
1.

Whether the petitioner Ansh suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 14.08.2023 at about 04.30 PM involving vehicle bearing registration No.
DL-1PC-6663 driven by Respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the Respondent no. 2 and insured with the Respondent No. 3?

OPP.
2.

Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation: If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. Relief.

The Grand father of petitioner filed an affidavit Ex PW1/A wherein he described the occurrence of incident in line with the facts mentioned in Para 1 of this award.
He deposed that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

PW-1 has relied upon the following documents viz:-

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.11.12 14:15:36 +0530 subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

As already discussed above, the father of petitioner examined himself as PW-1 in order to prove the factual averments regarding the occurrence of accident.

PW-1 has clearly and categorically stated that at the relevant time, the petitioner was in process to board the bus bearing registration no. DL-1PC-6663 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") suddenly the driver of the offending vehicle/ R-1 closed the gate of the bus negligently and moved the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and as a result of petitioner fell down on the road and his left leg and ankle crushed by the offending vehicle.

It is further stated that the the injured was admitted in BJRM hospital by the Duty Marshal of the offending vehicle from where he was referred to LNJP Hospital where the surgery was performed in his left leg.
It is further stated that the said accident was caused due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver / R-1 who closed the door negligently and drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
He was cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for R-3/ Insurance Company.
However, nothing favourable came to respondents.
by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA

The very fact that R-1 has already been chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279/338 IPC in the above criminal case/FIR in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW1 and the case of petitioner on this issue.

The copies of FIR, Chargesheet, Site plan, Mechanical inspection reports of offending vehicle, MLC, Seizure Memos, Arrest Memo of R-1 also corroborate the oral testimony of PW1.
12.

Besides the above, R-1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the depositions being made by PW1 regarding the above accident and its manner etc.,
but he has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
13.

14. Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of R-1,
if any, at the relevant time.

Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which the offending vehicle hit the Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.11.12 14:15:47 +0530 petitioner at the relevant time.

In the absence of any evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner at the relevant time, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 at the relevant time.
In totality, R-1 could not bring on record any material which reflects inconsistency in the oral testimony of PW-1.
As such, this Tribunal finds it appropriate to hold that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.

In view of the medical treatment documents available on record, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner in the above accident.
16. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries on his person on account of neglect and default of R-1 at the relevant time.
This issue thus stands decided against the respondents and in favour of the petitioner.
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?"
PANKAJ
SHARMA

As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
Here it would be appropriate to mention that the petitioner was a minor on the date of accident.

As such, the matter requires decision in accordance with the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited and Ors.
MANU/SC/0878/2013.

The relevant part of the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mallikarjun (supra) is extracted below :-
"12.

Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts,
we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, Rs. 3 lakhs; upto 60%, Rs. 4 lakhs; upto 90%, Rs. 5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs. 6 lakhs.
For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Rs. 1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick......."

(iv) Loss of Marriage Prospects 22.
Admittedly, petitioner had to undergo a lot of trauma and pain on account of the above accident when he was just 11 years old.
He also suffered a permanent disability to the extent of 40% with respect to his left lower limb.

This Tribunal could not turn a blind eye to the fact that the above disability is very much likely to affect the marriage prospects of the petitioner, given the existing social norms of our society at large.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries suffered by him which had impacted his future marriage prospects to a greater extent, petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- under this head as well.

opennyai_summary.facts:
A DAR was filed on 06/01/2024 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of the parties.
Subsequent to filing of DAR present petition U/s 166 r/w Section 140 of M.V. Act was seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 30 Lakhs in respect of injuries sustained by petitioner in a road traffic accident which took place on 14/08/2023 at about 4.30 PM at a spot Outer Ring Road, Service Road near Wazirabad Flyover falling within the jurisdiction of PS Wazirabad was filed.
As per this petition, at the relevant time the petitioner was in process to board the bus bearing registration no.
DL-1PC-6663 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") suddenly the driver of the offending vehicle/ R-1 closed the gate of the bus negligently and moved the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and as a result of petitioner fell down on the road and his left leg and ankle crushed by the offending vehicle.

Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation: If so, to what amount and from whom?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.11.12 14:15:36 +0530 subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

if any, at the relevant time.
In the absence of any evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner at the relevant time, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 at the relevant time.
In totality, R-1 could not bring on record any material which reflects inconsistency in the oral testimony of PW-1.
